item.title: Updates on HEIR, the Homomorphic Encryption Compiler Project
item.description:
📝 Assuming you won’t read the linked corporate blog post, HEIR is a compiler that converts an input program to a program that operates directly on encrypted data. I’ll try to say more about when and where this is useful later in this article. This model is small enough that bootstrapping (the slowest part of HE) is not required.
🔗 Read more: https://www.jeremykun.com/2026/09/04/updates-on-heir-homomorphic-encryption/

item.title: "Next-token predictor" is the wrong mental model for LLMs
item.description:
📝 During pre-training, the model learns only from sequences that already exist in the training data. During pre-training, it makes an actual_next_token more likely because that token appeared in the training data. That is a next-move predictor.
🔗 Read more: https://gmcgoldr.github.io/2026/09/04/llm-next-token-predictors.html
